opening.argument: Judge, consider the return claim alongside the action the description invites. The speaker measures a possible 10x for AVAX, then presents 832% and 511% retracement scenarios as more likely. The description invites viewers to join a crypto school and check out a trading signal. Those links do not explicitly instruct viewers to buy AVAX, but they give viewers a way to engage with a promoted trading offering immediately after hearing large upside figures. That connection deserves more scrutiny than the chart analysis alone.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense is right that the speaker does not guarantee a 10x and says the timing is unknown. But its account leaves out the description's invitations to join the school and check the signal. Risk disclosures address uncertainty; they do not remove the promotional role those invitations can play when placed beside substantial upside scenarios. The question is whether the analysis also steers viewers toward a trading-related offering.

opening.argument: Judge, the signals are concerning in combination. The title foregrounds a 10x recovery. In the analysis, the speaker asks whether viewers would be happy with an 832% retracement and calls a 511% retracement more likely. The description then points to a trading signal and a hardware-wallet discount. None of those facts alone proves deception, and the video includes risk language. Together, though, they create an upside-focused presentation with routes into crypto-related products. The disclaimer should be weighed against that overall impression, not treated as the end of the inquiry.

opening.argument: Judge, this can function as promotion even while using the vocabulary of technical analysis. The speaker says a 302% move has happened repeatedly and is more likely going forward; he also describes higher price levels as easier to reach after key barriers break. The description offers a crypto school and a trading signal, while separately acknowledging that promotional relationships may bring compensation. That does not prove a paid relationship for this video or an instruction to buy AVAX. It does give the judge reason to examine whether the educational framing is also building interest in speculative participation.
